title: Predicate
definition: A predicate is an expression that evaluates a proposition to a Boolean result for a given input or state.
purpose: Give meaningful names and contracts to individual decision questions.
history: Predicates connect formal logic with program conditions by representing properties or relationships as truth-valued expressions.
mental_model: A predicate is a yes/no question asked of current input or state.
analogy: A checklist question can be answered yes or no; the analogy fails if the question is vague or depends on hidden state.
relationships: can be combined by logical operators
common_mistakes: Combining multiple questions in one predicate
industry_notes: Named predicates reduce duplicated rules and make reviews/tests speak in domain language.
ai_notes: AI may invent hidden assumptions inside predicates; require explicit input and rule contracts.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to decompose a dense condition into named predicates.
exercise_candidates: Name predicates for an access policy
